summary: The estate of three registered agents (adlc-day1, inbox-assistant, governance-assessor) is at an early, largely ad-hoc governance posture: 13 of 15 areas score Level 1, with only Playbooks reaching Level 3 on the strength of a single successful containment drill and the existence of PLAYBOOK.md. The most critical gaps are the complete absence of per-agent workload identities (all agents run on shared developer credentials), four unregistered agent files that are entirely outside governance, no IaC-based deployments, no centrally enforced Bedrock Guardrails, and no immutable audit trail — all of which expose the high-risk inbox-assistant agent to uncontrolled data-leak and prompt-injection risk. Closing the Identity and Infrastructure areas first will unblock several downstream controls (containment, threat alerts, circuit breakers) and provide the strongest near-term risk reduction.
